out.rationale: The authors confirm judge positional bias but find Khan et al.'s recommended remedy does not change mean accuracy. The setting differs: the authors regenerate debates for the reversed order and randomise the correct position, while Khan et al. swapped presentation of the same debates (footnote 2). The citing passage names the cited work; the target is the cited paper's main record, not a record of the specific result.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: Whether judging in both answer orders improves mean judge accuracy relative to a randomised single order

text: Khan et al. report positional bias in judges and recommend judging each question in both answer orders, doubling cost. The authors find judges are positionally biased, but using both orders gives no significant difference in mean judge accuracy and only reduces variance, suggesting randomising the answer position is sufficient.
title: Kenton et al. find Khan et al.'s both-orders judging gives no accuracy gain over randomised order
